title: Finiteness lifts along finite order thickenings
statement: Let $S\subseteq S'$ be a finite order thickening of schemes [def-sbc-first-order-thickening] (a closed subscheme whose quasi-coherent ideal sheaf $\mathcal I\subseteq\mathcal O_{S'}$ satisfies $\mathcal I^{n+1}=0$ for some $n$), let $f':X'\to S'$ be a morphism of schemes and let $f:X=S\times_{S'}X'\to S$ be its base change [def-pc-base-change]. Then $f$ is finite if and only if $f'$ is finite [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism].

source.place: More on Morphisms, Lemma 09ZW (label lemma-thicken-property-morphisms-cartesian), part (8), with its proof (first paragraph and 'Proof of (8)')

proof.text: ($f'$ finite $\Rightarrow$ $f$ finite.) $f:X=S\times_{S'}X'\to S$ is the base change of $f'$ along $S\to S'$, and finite morphisms are stable under base change (Morphisms, Lemma 01WL); so $f$ is finite. It remains to show the converse, 'the interesting direction'.

source.place: More on Morphisms, Lemma 09ZW, proof, first paragraph ('The properties listed in the lemma are all stable under base change ... Morphisms, Lemma ... base-change-finite')

proof.text: Choose n with i.ker^(n+1) = 0. Mathlib Scheme.IdealSheafData.support_pow_succ and support_bot give i.ker.support = the whole target. Scheme.Hom.support_ker identifies this support with the closure of the range; since i is a closed immersion its range is closed, so i is surjective. Both closed immersions and surjective scheme morphisms are stable under base change (the two cited Mathlib leaves), so pullback.fst f' i is a thickening. The square commutes by pullback.condition. This constructs the morphism of thickenings required in step 4 without introducing universal homeomorphisms.

proof.text: ($f'$ is integral.) By step 2, $(f,f')$ is a morphism of thickenings, and $f$ is integral by step 3; hence $f'$ is integral by More on Morphisms 09ZV (5).

source.place: More on Morphisms, Lemma 09ZW, proof, 'Proof of (8)' ('results of Lemma 09ZV'), i.e. Lemma 09ZV part (5)

proof.text: ($f'$ is locally of finite type.) $S\subseteq S'$ is a finite order thickening and $X=S\times_{S'}X'$, and $f$ is locally of finite type by step 3; hence $f'$ is locally of finite type by part (2) of the same lemma 09ZW. The local finite type lemma is stated for pullback.fst i f', whereas this theorem uses pullback.snd f' i. Precompose the latter with (pullbackSymmetry i f').hom, an isomorphism; pullbackSymmetry_hom_comp_snd and stability of local finite type under composition identify the resulting locally finite type map with pullback.fst i f'. Apply the cited equivalence to it.
